relevance.rationale: WRONG JOIN. The seeded id was gasper-rahman-2004, whose ref() entry (references.ts:482) is a two-volume-style monograph on basic hypergeometric series. This document is a short single-author journal article, arXiv:1105.1998v3 [math.CA], SIGMA 7 (2011) paper 115, 11 pages, deriving a connection formula for the Hahn-Exton q-Bessel function between the origin and infinity via the q-Borel and q-Laplace transformations, and taking the p -> 1^- limit of that formula. It is not the monograph and the join must be broken. No existing ref() key matches it: grep of references.ts for '1105.1998' and for the author name returns nothing (the only same-surname key is an unrelated 1981 quaternionic Standard-Model entry), so id is null. In its own right this is CORE for the folio, which is why the mis-join is costly: the corpus already runs a Hahn-Exton q-Bessel identification programme (references.ts entries around lines 385-441 on E_q(2) matrix coefficients, q-Bessel zeros and q-Lommel recurrences, the self-reciprocal q-Hankel transform; QBesselContiguityRecurrence.lean; KeystoneSelfDualSpectralNarrowing.lean) AND a q-Borel/q-Laplace summability programme (QOU/Mathlib/QGevreyOrder.lean, QAlienBridgeEquation.lean, QOU/Archimedean/BalancedKernelConfluence.lean, which cites divizio-zhang2009 for exactly the q -> 1 confluence route). This document sits precisely at the intersection of those two: q-Borel/q-Laplace applied to the Hahn-Exton q-Bessel, with the confluence limit taken explicitly. Corpus-grep for a prior claim on this ground: docs/audits/ and docs/coordination/ contain no entry for arXiv 1105.1998, and no content/ block cites it, so nothing here re-declares a closed item.

keyResults.statement: A connection formula relating the Hahn-Exton q-Bessel function's behaviour at the origin and at infinity, obtained by q-Borel and q-Laplace transformation, together with its confluent limit as the base tends to 1 from below.
keyResults.useForFolio: The corpus's q-Bessel work and its q-Borel/confluence work are currently separate literature legs; this supplies the connection-formula bridge between them, and the explicit base -> 1 limit is the same confluence route BalancedKernelConfluence.lean cites divizio-zhang2009 for. Reading it may sharpen the q-Bessel contiguity/recurrence derivation, though I have NOT checked whether its normalisation matches the corpus's J_nu(x;q) convention — that check is a precondition for any use.

proposedActions.rationale: The document is directly on two active fronts (Hahn-Exton q-Bessel identification, q-Borel/q-Laplace confluence) and has no ref() entry. Create one before anything cites it; the ledger row must carry id null until then so the false join to the monograph key is not propagated.

Before citing it anywhere, its Hahn-Exton normalisation must be reconciled with the corpus's convention recorded in the gasper-rahman-2004 note (J_nu(x;q) = x^nu (q^{nu+1};q)_inf/(q;q)_inf . 1phi1(0; q^{nu+1}; q, q x^2)). A connection formula in a different normalisation is not transferable, and adopting one because its numbers look right would be a fit.
